output.brief:
The rise in cancellations is mostly not a pricing problem. It comes from the Quillbook accounting connector. Quillbook retired its old invoice interface on 30 March. Since then the connector has silently dropped or duplicated invoices: 58,300 invoices across 1,212 of 1,900 connected accounts. About 34% of those accounts have cancelled, against 8% of Quillbook accounts with no recorded failure. Quillbook-connected accounts churn at about 6% a month whether or not they are repriced. Founders accounts, who kept the old price, churn just as much. Accounts with no connector, which are most of the base, are essentially unchanged at about 1.9%. The earlier seat-band pattern reflects the fact that larger accounts are more likely to use Quillbook. I'm fairly confident, but the churn comparison was not adjusted for other differences between accounts.

What to do next: make the Quillbook v3 fix the top engineering priority (3–4 weeks). Contact all Quillbook-connected accounts, including those that cancelled, to correct their invoices. Keep the duplicate-invoice hold, because it has stopped 3,870 duplicates reaching customers' books. Don't roll back the price: it would cost about $220k a month and wouldn't address the cause. Hold off on the Tallymarsh rebuild. Instead, review the Tallymarsh logs, which haven't been looked at yet. Also fix the monitoring so it counts WARN-level failures.
